successors.name: Portuguese Angola
successors.text: the Mbundu highlands between the Lukala and the Kwanza that Portugal took in 1671: Bengo, Cuanza Norte and the Lukala side of Malanje Province (Pungo Andongo), without the Luanda disc and the Kwanza…

ledger.x: 1518: Ngola Kiluanji sends ambassadors to Portugal; the infobox 'Established' date for Ndongo.
1582: the Portuguese found Massangano on the Kwanza.
1602: Portugal founds the presidio of Cambambe on the Kwanza, after Ndongo and Portugal 'formalized their border' in 1599.
1617: Governor Luis Mendes de Vasconcelos 'sacked the capital' and forced Ngola Mbandi to flee to Kindonga.
1626: the Portuguese install a rival king.
1626: Ndongo becomes a Portuguese client under Hari a Kiluanji.
1626: the seat moves to Pungo a Ndongo.
1641: Nzinga, allied with the Dutch, begins retaking Ndongo.
1670-1671: Filipe revolts and the client kingdom ends.
1671: Ndongo's last fortress falls and the kingdom ends.

wars.name: Portuguese war on Ndongo (Dias de Novais to the 1599 border)
wars.outcome: Ngola Ndambi ambushed Portuguese forces in 1579-1580; a Kongo invasion was 'narrowly defeated in 1580'; the Portuguese founded Massangano in 1582 and were crushed at Kabasa in 1590 after Ndongo allied with Matamba; Ndongo and Portugal formalized their border…

wars.name: Vasconcelos expedition against Ndongo
wars.outcome: Kabasa was sacked in 1617 and Ngola Mbandi fled to Kindonga; a peace treaty was negotiated in 1621-1622 and Nzinga returned to Kabasa in late 1622.

wars.name: Nzinga's wars against Portugal
wars.outcome: The Portuguese declared war on Nzinga on 15 March 1626 and installed Hari a Kiluanji; she fled in 1627-1628, took Matamba in 1631, reclaimed large parts of Ndongo with Dutch help in 1641-1644, won at Kombi in 1647; peace in late 1656 and a treaty of 1657…

wars.name: Revolt of Filipe Hari a Ngola
wars.outcome: Filipe revolted against the Portuguese; his fortress fell in 1671 and Ndongo ended as an independent kingdom.

certainty.note: No boundary is given by the pages.
The Ndongo-Portugal border was 'formalized' in 1599 but the page (re-read in the fix pass) does not say where it ran, so no sharp line can be drawn.
